key_insight: Randomized orthogonal mixing and progressive residual-sign coding enable training-free Transformer weight compression with fidelity improving as residual stages are added.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers flexible storage–fidelity trade-offs without learned codebooks, empirical CDFs, or trellis optimization.
method: Orthogonally mix residuals to promote Gaussian-like distributions for sign coding.
Independently normalize and analytically calibrate reconstruction at each residual stage.
Progressively encode residual errors to refine reconstructed weights.
evidence_signal: Across attention and MLP projections, five-stage joint quantization achieved perplexities of 32.16 on GPT-2 Large and 12.73 on Llama-3-8B, versus full-precision baselines of 29.89 and 11.07.
watch_item: Predictive fidelity remains below full precision, and deployment should account for residual-stage storage overhead and runtime trade-offs.
paper_title: Orthogonally Mixed Sign Coding with Progressive Residual Refinement for Transformer Weight Compression
